subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should OpenAI support reuse the existing cache-TTL eligibility and TTL semantics, or should this issue wait for a provider-agnostic or retention-aware pruning design?
rationale: Current source proves the OpenAI gate gap, but enabling it changes runtime behavior for existing OpenAI configs and prior PR review flagged retention/session-state semantics that code inspection alone cannot settle.

options.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
options.body: Require the linked PR or a replacement to document the OpenAI pruning policy, preserve explicit user TTL behavior, add focused tests, and include redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Accept current cache-TTL semantics
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept that existing OpenAI `cache-ttl` configs become active under the generic TTL, trading compatibility caution for a narrow eligibility fix.

options.title: Pursue provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Close or pause the current eligibility PR and implement a separate pruning mode that does not depend on prompt-cache eligibility.

recommendation.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR or a replacement to document the OpenAI pruning policy, preserve explicit user TTL behavior, add focused tests, and include redacted native OpenAI idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest release commit introduced the shipped cache-TTL helper/test surface, so this owner is the best available routing candidate for the provider eligibility decision.
